content.text:
**The Mom Test** is a customer-discovery approach for figuring out whether your business idea is actually good—by asking questions that even your mom couldn’t politely lie about.

The core idea: **don’t ask people whether your idea is good. Ask about their real past behavior, problems, and spending.**

Bad questions:

- “Do you like my app idea?”
- “Would you use this?”
- “Would you pay $10/month for it?”
- “Do you think this is a good business?”

People often say yes to be nice, speculative, or encouraging.

Better Mom Test questions:

- “How do you currently solve this problem?”
- “When was the last time that happened?”
- “What did you try?”
- “How much time or money did it cost you?”
- “Who else is involved in solving it?”
- “Have you paid for anything to fix this?”
- “What happens if you don’t solve it?”

The rule of thumb:

> **Talk about their life, not your idea. Talk about specifics, not hypotheticals. Listen more than you pitch.**

For example, instead of saying:

> “Would you use an app that helps you meal plan?”

Ask:

> “How do you currently plan meals?”
> “When did you last do that?”
> “What’s annoying about it?”
> “Have you tried any apps, spreadsheets, or services?”
> “What made you stop using them?”

The goal is to learn whether the problem is **real, frequent, painful, and worth paying to solve**—before you waste time building the wrong thing.
